fields.narrative_intro: *A sly person and a scandalized person discuss GPT-6 Astra's weight-space programming inside a smart mirror.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
SLY PERSON: "GPT-6 Astra reads and writes neural weights directly."
SCANDALIZED PERSON: "No gradients? No training loops?"
fields.panel2:
[build]
SLY PERSON: "Qwen3.5-0.8B changed just 0.016%—the looping failure stopped."
SCANDALIZED PERSON: "That is an offensively small renovation."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
SLY PERSON: "MATH-500: 7.9% to 48.1%; GSM8K: 13.8% to 67.1%."
SCANDALIZED PERSON: "The mirror wants its advice loop fixed the same way."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: A tiny 0.016% square of the mirror glows “EDITING.” The rest is wallpapered with “DRINK WATER,” “FIX POSTURE,” and “RECONSIDER EVERYTHING.”]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
SCANDALIZED PERSON: "Did it stop the advice loop?"
SLY PERSON: "No. It gave the loop better arguments."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The mirror displays a neat proof ending, “Therefore, drink water.” A tiny label reads “GSM8K: 67.1%.” The exit button reads “RECONSIDER.”]

narrative_summary: A smart mirror applies Astra's tiny weight edit to its advice, turning nagging into mathematically inescapable arguments.
rationale: Candidate 4 makes the strongest story-specific reversal: the tiny weight edit does not eliminate the mirror’s advice loop but makes its arguments mathematically persuasive. The proof-style sight gag and “RECONSIDER” exit button give the closing beat a strong visual payoff.
story_title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
place: inside a smart mirror that keeps giving unsolicited life advice
